jobs.description:
About MFAN

The Military Family Advisory Network (MFAN) is a national nonprofit organization that conducts rigorous research, develops responsive programs, and brings together military families, government, nonprofit, and private-sector partners to drive meaningful change. MFAN is entering an important period of growth and transformation as we implement a new strategic plan, strengthen our national positioning, expand the reach of our research and programs, and prepare for a rebrand and website redesign. 

The Opportunity

MFAN seeks a seasoned, strategic Director of Communications to lead an integrated, enterprise-wide communications function. This is not solely a content-production or media-relations role. The Director will establish a multi-channel communications plan, systems, standards, and team practices that enable MFAN to communicate with greater clarity, consistency, and influence as the organization grows. 

Reporting initially to the Chief Executive Officer, the Director will translate complex research, program impact, policy priorities, and the lived experiences of military families into compelling communications for diverse audiences. The Director of Communications will be counted on to delegate and lead a team, while managing a budget and discerning when it is appropriate to bring in outside support for specialized, tactical elements. The Director will be MFAN's senior communications advisor, lead major organizational initiatives, and manage staff, contractors, agencies, budgets, and workflows. The ideal candidate is both a strong strategist and an excellent operator: someone who can set the direction, build the plan, guide others, and step in personally when the moment requires it. 

This is a consequential role; the Director of Communications must have excellent judgement and understand the content, stakeholders, and environment that MFAN operates in. A growth mentality is a must.

What Success Looks like in the First Year

  • Build and begin implementing a multiyear communications strategy aligned with MFAN's 2027–2030 strategic plan and organizational goals. 
  • Create an integrated editorial and campaign-planning system that aligns research, programs, government relations, advancement, events, and executive communications. 
  • Strengthen MFAN's national visibility and reputation as a trusted, nonpartisan source of military family insight and solutions. 
  • Develop a disciplined approach to translating MFAN's data, evidence, and impact into accessible narratives for families, funders, policymakers, partners, media, and the public. 
  • Assess and strengthen the communications team structure, vendor portfolio, workflows, measures of success, and quality-control practices. 
  • In coordination with leaders across the organization, develop and implement the personnel, technology, and systems infrastructure needed to advance strategic priorities, align resources with the budget, and strengthen organizational efficiency, productivity, and quality—not just for the communications area, but for the full organization. 
  • Lead communications planning and execution for MFAN's rebrand and website redesign, in close partnership with executive leadership and external specialists. 

Position Type / Hours of Work

  • Full-Time, Exempt Position
  • Hours: Standard hours of operation are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET on Monday–Thursday and 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. ET on Fridays, unless otherwise approved by the department lead. There will be occasions when extended hours are required due to events, travel, meetings, or other requirements.
  • Location: Remote. As this is a fully remote position, candidates are expected to have a dedicated workspace and access to high-speed internet. This position is limited to a candidate living in the 48 contiguous states and must have regular availability during Eastern Time business hours.
  • Travel: Travel is required for conferences, partner meetings, MFAN events, and staff retreats (monthly travel should be expected).  

Duties & Responsibilities

Enterprise Communications Strategy and Leadership 

  • Develop and own an integrated communications strategy that advances MFAN's mission, strategic plan, reputation, growth, and impact. 
  • Serve as a senior advisor to the CEO and executive leadership team on messaging, organizational positioning, reputation, emerging issues, and communications opportunities. 
  • Establish clear annual priorities, audience strategies, campaign plans, performance measures, decision rights, and cross-functional workflows. 
  • Design, implement, and maintain organization-wide communications efforts and operating rhythms in close coordination with research, programs, fundraising, government relations, and events leaders, ensuring that priorities are aligned and work moves forward with clear ownership and accountability. 
  • Lead through organizational change, helping staff understand and consistently communicate MFAN's evolving strategy, identity, priorities, and value. 

Brand, Messaging, and Digital Transformation 

  • Steward MFAN's brand and ensure consistent use of its voice, messages, narrative, and visual identity across the organization. 
  • Lead communications strategy and internal coordination for MFAN's rebrand and website redesign, including audience needs, content architecture, editorial standards, launch planning, and adoption. 
  • Maintain a reliable source of approved messages, evidence, proof points, and organizational language for use across communications, fundraising, partnerships, and public engagement. 
  • Oversee MFAN's website, email, social media, digital campaigns, and other external channels, using data to improve reach, engagement, and conversion. 

Research Translation, Thought Leadership, and Storytelling 

  • Partner closely with research and impact leaders to translate complex findings into clear, accurate, timely, and actionable communications without compromising rigor. 
  • Develop thought-leadership strategies that position MFAN and its subject-matter experts for media commentary, speaking opportunities, op-eds, convenings, and other influential platforms. 
  • Create a balanced narrative approach that combines credible data, program outcomes, partner contributions, and the lived experiences of military families. 
  • Guide communications for major research releases, national events, program launches, and rapid-response moments. 

Media, Executive, and Public Communications 

  • Build and sustain relationships with national, military, policy, trade, and local media; identify timely opportunities and develop proactive pitches. 
  • Prepare the CEO and other subject-matter experts for interviews, speeches, panels, testimony, and high-visibility engagements. 
  • Draft or oversee executive communications, public statements, talking points, opinion pieces, presentations, and sensitive organizational messages. 
  • Develop practical issues-management and crisis communication protocols and lead communications when rapid coordination is required. 

Advancement, Partner, and Program Communications 

  • Partner with advancement to ensure donor and corporate-partner communications are compelling, accurate, consistent, and aligned with MFAN's broader narrative. 
  • Support the development of cases for support, proposals, stewardship materials, sponsorship campaigns, reports, and other high-value communications while maintaining clear ownership between communications and fundraising. 
  • Collaborate with programs and government relations to reach military families, partners, policymakers, and community stakeholders with audience-specific communications. 
  • Lead communications planning for partner campaigns while protecting MFAN's credibility, nonpartisan voice, and brand standards. 

Team, Operations, and Performance 

  • Lead, coach, and develop communications staff while creating clear expectations, accountability, and opportunities for growth. 
  • Select and manage agencies, consultants, designers, producers, freelancers, and other vendors; oversee scopes, timelines, budgets, quality, and results. 
  • Build repeatable systems for intake, prioritization, editorial planning, production, review, approval, asset management, and performance reporting. 
  • Use analytics and audience insight to evaluate results, communicate progress, and continuously improve strategy and execution. 
  • Manage the communications budget and make thoughtful decisions about internal capacity, external support, and resource allocation. 

Required Experience & Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.
  • At least eight years of progressively responsible experience in strategic communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, public affairs, or a related field, including meaningful experience leading a communications function or major portfolio. 
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing integrated communications strategies tied to organizational priorities and measurable outcomes. 
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex priorities, adapt quickly to changing needs, and deliver polished, high-quality work in a fast-paced environment. 
  • A collaborative, no-ego leadership style and the ability to build trust and accountability across functions in a remote organization. 
  • Experience leading staff and managing consultants, agencies, vendors, budgets, and simultaneous high-stakes projects. 
  • Experience leading a significant brand, messaging, website, or organizational-positioning initiative through planning, stakeholder alignment, implementation, and adoption. 
  • Exceptional writing, editing, message-development, and storytelling skills across executive, media, digital, donor, partner, and public-facing formats. 
  • Strong record of translating complex information, research, or policy into accessible and compelling content while protecting accuracy and nuance. 
  • Sound judgment and the ability to advise senior leaders, navigate sensitive issues, manage competing perspectives, and make decisions in a fast-moving environment. 
  • Commitment to MFAN's mission, nonpartisan approach, and responsibility to represent military families with accuracy, dignity, and respect. 

Preferred Skills

  • Experience in a national nonprofit, research, policy, public affairs, association, or other mission-driven organization. 
  • Experience communicating research findings or supporting advocacy, public policy, or systems-change efforts. 
  • Familiarity with military and veteran communities, military family policy, or the national-security ecosystem. Military affiliation is welcomed but not required. 
  • Experience supporting fundraising, corporate partnerships, sponsorships, or cause-marketing initiatives. 
  • Experience with modern content management, email, social media, project management, and analytics platforms. Familiarity with specific software is less important than the ability to select and use tools strategically. 

Benefits

We’re proud to offer a comprehensive and people-centered benefits package designed to support your well-being both in and out of work:

  • Health & Wellness: QSEHRA (Qualified Small Employer Health Reimbursement Arrangement) to help cover your health insurance and medical expenses.
  • Technology Allotment: MFAN offers monthly technology reimbursement or stipend.
  • Time to Recharge: Generous vacation days, sick leave, and compassionate leave—because life happens.
  • Summer Fridays: Enjoy shortened hours on Fridays during the summer months.
  • 401K: Available immediately upon hire with a 3% employer match.

We believe in flexibility, care, and supporting our team with meaningful benefits that promote balance and sustainability.

Working Conditions

The work environment described here is representative of those an employee encounter while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable

individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The qualified employee will work in a

dynamic home office setting, and interact with staff and consultants, and therefore may be subjected to

interruptions throughout the workday. The position will require some flexible hours, and when

applicable, local and national travel will be required.

Location & Work Authorization

This position is open only to candidates who are legally authorized to work in the United States and who will perform all work from within the United States. MFAN does not sponsor employment visas or assume sponsorship of existing employment visas, now or in the future.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Why We Exist

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace.

We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and became profitable in early 2024. We're now expanding into adjacent verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, etc) to become the one-stop-shop for all your physical assets.

Why We’re Hiring

Our Data Science & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a Data Science team member embedded within it — someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years.

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Data Science team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

  • Growth Marketing

  • Product Development

  • Strategic Partnerships

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

  • No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc.

  • No corporate fluff: The Data Science & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals.

  • Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end.

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Data Science & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

  • Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

  • Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

  • Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

Who You Are

  • First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?"

  • Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

  • Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

What You'll Bring

  • 1+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

  • Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

  • Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

  • Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

As an Account Executive at HubSpot, you use outbound selling strategies to find new business and help them grow using HubSpot software. You run online demos of the HubSpot software and successfully sell the HubSpot value proposition. Your target clients will largely consist of small businesses. This position would be based out of your home office working in an inside sales model, and it is a full closing role.

We are actively hiring for a Small Business Account Executive; candidates are eligible to be office, flex or remotely located in the Republic of Ireland based on individual preference! Please check out this article for more context: The Future of Work at HubSpot: How We're Building a Hybrid Company.

What are the responsibilities of a Account Executive at HubSpot?

In this role, you will get to:

  • Quickly identify challenges that our prospective customers face and discover the best inbound marketing solutions for their business
  • Consistently close new business at or above quota level
  • Nurture relationships with highly qualified opportunities at small and mid-sized companies
  • Build relationships with prospects and internal stakeholders to grow new business

  • Strong communication, time management and adaptability in order to be set up for success remotely
  • Experience working in a high-growth, "scale up" environment
  • Passion for helping businesses grow and curiosity about the tech industry
  • Humility and enthusiasm in their work

  • Interactive employee training and onboarding

Jerry is expanding into several new markets at the same time. Capital allocation is now one of the most consequential decisions we make: each dollar committed to a new product line, a marketing channel, or a headcount is a dollar not available elsewhere.

We are hiring a Strategic Finance Manager, reporting to our VP of Finance, to build the analysis those decisions rest on. You will own the operating model and the planning cycle, partner with functional leaders across the company, and work closely with the CFO and the founders.

What You’ll Own

The operating core is the model, the planning cadence, and the spend discipline the company runs on. Alongside it, you are the analytical partner on new opportunities — the products, verticals, channels and partnerships we are deciding whether to back. And over your first year or two, as our newer products scale and the audience for our numbers widens beyond the people who already know the business, the reporting itself has to reach a standard that holds up to outside diligence.

  • Direct communicator: You form a view, communicate it directly, and revise it when the evidence changes.

  • Executive-ready output: What you produce can go in front of the founders or the board without a rewrite — clear, precise, and honest about what the numbers do and do not show.

  • Owner: You take ownership of outcomes and are comfortable building process where none exists yet.

  • 4+ years of relevant experience, ideally combining 2+ years at a reputable investment bank, corporate development group, or private equity firm with 2+ years in strategic finance or FP&A at a high-growth company.

  • A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a similarly quantitative field.

  • Strong financial modeling skills: driver-based operating models, three-statement mechanics, scenario and sensitivity analysis, and a working command of accounting concepts and GAAP.

  • Experience with unit economics in a consumer or marketplace business, including CAC, LTV, payback, cohort retention, and contribution margin.

  • A track record of translating complex analysis into a clear narrative for an executive or investor audience.

  • Startup or high-growth experience strongly preferred, including building financial processes from scratch.

jobs.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Mission

You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast.

As a Senior Project Manager, you make large, global blp transformations happen. These programs touch finance, procurement and supply chain at once, run across multiple ERP systems and legal entities, and roll out country by country. Your job is to orchestrate all of it and get the customer live: the first go-live above all, because that is where credibility is won or lost, and then wave after wave with the same discipline. You run the steering committee, you lead a blp team on each engagement, and you do that across several engagements at once.

At both levels, scope is the single biggest lever on whether a project goes live on time. Protecting it is a daily job, not a contract clause. You escalate early and precisely rather than absorbing problems until they become critical.

You will not be alone with the technical side. Integrations Engineers handle the connection into the ERP, Technical Project Managers handle the harder solution design, and our Consultants take over the automation work after go-live. On our largest strategic accounts a Client Partner carries the relationship and the commercial number, so your attention goes to delivery quality.

We have done this many times, so you are not inventing the approach each time. A proven onboarding method and a strong toolkit are what let you carry your own customers from early on.

Your Career Path in Project Management

This is the path most of our delivery leadership came through, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the size of the programs you have delivered, and we are explicit about what the next step requires.

  • Project Manager: You get customers live end to end, several in parallel: guided onboarding for commercial customers, leading enterprise projects yourself, or a workstream on our largest programs. Typically you bring 2+ years in consulting, implementation or project management.

  • Senior Project Manager: You make large, global transformations happen: multiple ERPs, entities and countries, the steering committee, and a blp team on each engagement. Typically you bring 5+ years delivering complex, multi-country programs.

  • Next steps: Lead a delivery team, or move into Consulting and from there towards our Client Partner role on strategic accounts.

Moves into Consulting or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run implementations end to end: kick-off, scope, planning, configuration, testing and go-live.

  • Manage several customers in parallel at different stages, and keep every one of them on date.

  • Work with customers on their processes, and flag early where a process assumption will not hold.

  • Coordinate the specialists on your projects: Integrations Engineers, Technical Project Managers and AI Automation Specialists.

  • Own scope actively. Recognize a change request for what it is and handle it deliberately.

  • Keep the project inside its budget, and raise it early when the effort is drifting.

  • Hand over cleanly at go-live to our Consultants and support organization.

Familiarity with DeltaV DCS, batch recipes and control modules is preferred, as is knowledge of 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11. Strong documentation and troubleshooting skills, and the ability to work independently and collaborate with cross-functional teams, are essential.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute Computer System Validation (CSV) protocols for Emerson DeltaV automation systems.
  • Draft detailed test scripts to validate DeltaV batch recipes, automation sequences, control logic, and system configurations.

jobs.excerpt: About Clarity PediatricsClarity Pediatricsisreimagining pediatric chronic care, starting with ADHD.
jobs.description:
About Clarity Pediatrics

Clarity Pediatricsisreimagining pediatric chronic care, starting with ADHD. Nearly 10% of children in the US are diagnosed with ADHD, and for parents, finding the right care can feel impossible. We're building a virtual pediatric ADHD clinic that delivers trusted, science-backed care to all families, and it's working. We have strong product-market fit, a growing patient base, and a clear path to expanding into other common chronic conditions like asthma, allergies, and obesity.

Our leadership team has deep healthcare expertise. Our CEO has led two startups to more than $100M in ARR and profitability. Our Chief Medical Officer trained at UCSF and Stanford and previously built specialty care services at Kaiser Permanente. Clarity is female-led: our CEO, Head of Engineering, and product leadership are all women building a company where diverse perspectives drive better care and better technology.

We've raised $14.5M in Series A capital from top VCs who have backed category-defining health-tech companies like One Medical, Hims, Spring Health, Cityblock, Honor, and Tia.

The role

Texas is where we want to invest and experiment most aggressively right now, and Dallas–Fort Worth is one of the markets where we start. We’re hiring a Physician Liaison to own the ground game: getting into pediatric practices across the market, earning the trust of the physicians and the front desk, and turning that into referrals.

This is a field job. You’ll be out five days a week in clinics, at the front desk, at lunches, and in hallways between patients. You’ll work a target list of pediatric practices, get past the door, get in front of the physician, and give them a reason to send us their next patient with anxiety, ADHD, or obesity.

We have a strong playbook from California and you’ll get it on day one. Clinical presentations with our own physicians activate new providers better than almost anything else we do. Layering touches inside a tight window is what makes a clinic activate. Expect the playbook to change as we learn Texas. The target list, the pitch, and the sequence will all move, and we want someone who treats that as normal and tells us straight what they are seeing in the field.

You’ll report to our Head of GTM today, and to our Growth General Manager once that role is in seat.

What success looks like in year one:

  • 200 referring clinics across Dallas–Fort Worth, actively sending patients

  • Hundreds of individual referring providers inside those clinics

  • Referral volume growing quarter over quarter across your territory

  • Relationships stable enough that a clinic keeps referring when you’re not standing in the lobby

What you’ll own

  • Activate new clinics Work a target list across Dallas and Fort Worth. Prospect cold, get past the front desk, book the meeting, and turn practices into referring partners. Run the territory like it’s your own book of business.

  • Run in-services Get in front of a whole practice, physicians and staff together, and teach them what Clarity treats, who to send, and how to send them. You deliver these yourself.

  • Grow the clinics you win The first referral is the start of the account. Build relationships with physicians, medical assistants, office managers, and referral coordinators until Clarity is the default place they send these patients.

  • Set up clinical presentations Find the practices worth a physician-led presentation, get them scheduled, and get our medical advisors and clinicians in the room. You build the opportunity, they deliver the content.

  • Document your work Log every account, contact, visit, and outcome in the CRM the same day it happens, following our field team’s conventions. Keep account records current, including who the referring providers are, where each practice stands, and what the next step is. Your records are how we decide where to spend the next dollar and the next rep, so they need to be complete and accurate rather than close enough.

  • Bring the market back to the team You’ll have a better read than anyone here on what lands with a Texas pediatrician. Bring it back on a regular cadence: what’s working, what objections you’re hearing, which materials fall flat, and what we should change. In a new market, why a clinic said no is worth as much to us as the ones that said yes.

What we’re looking for

  • 2+ years in healthcare sales or provider relations You’ve called on physician practices and grown referrals. Pediatrics or behavioral health is a plus. A track record of hitting or beating a number is what we will look for first.

  • A clinical background is a real advantage If you are a nurse, an MA, or came up on the care delivery side and moved into sales, you will be more credible in these rooms and we will weight that heavily.

  • You work fast and you carry a lot at once You’d rather get through twenty practices than perfect one. Hearing no all week doesn’t wear you down.

  • You can walk into a room cold The front desk is the hardest door in this job. It is a learnable skill, but you have to want to do it.

  • You can present to a full practice In-services mean standing in front of a room of physicians and staff and holding their attention for fifteen minutes.

  • You’re disciplined about documentation You keep a CRM current without being asked, and you’ve worked in Salesforce, Zoho, or something like them.

  • You learn fast and take coaching We’ll teach you the clinical material and the playbook. You need to pick it up quickly, run it the way we ask, and tell us where it breaks.

  • Based in Dallas–Fort Worth Valid driver’s license, clean driving record, and reliable transportation. You’ll be driving the metroplex every day, with one to three trips a year to the SF Bay Area for onboarding and team on-sites.

Compensation, equity & location

  • Total on-target earnings of $112,000 to $128,000, made up of:

  • Base salary of $70,000 to 80,000

  • On-target variable compensation of $42,000 to $48,000 tied to referral growth in your territory. Variable is paid quarterly, and pay is set individually based on track record; there is no cap on the variable compensation

  • Guaranteed variable payout in your first full quarter while you ramp and build the territory

  • Equity in an early-stage, well-funded company

  • Mileage reimbursed at the IRS standard rate

  • Medical, dental, vision, and ancillary benefits, plus 401(k)

  • Paid holidays and flexible PTO

  • Full-time W-2, based in Dallas–Fort Worth, four to five days per week in the field

  • Reports to our Growth General Manager

  • Candidates must be authorized to work in the US without the need for company sponsorship

jobs.excerpt: The PCB Design Specialist designs and develops complex detailed layouts of printed circuit boards.
jobs.description:
The PCB Design Specialist designs and develops complex detailed layouts of printed circuit boards. Collaborates in developing state-of-the-art designs of new or modified, RF printed circuit boards. Establishes design standards and configurations. Works from preliminary schematics, part lists and basic description of the board function, configuration and arrangement as defined by engineering. May perform the checking of design layouts and detailed drawings. This position is remote. Legal authorization to work in the US is required.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Create PCB/PCBA design using Altium software with input from both mechanical and electrical
  • Create schematics and modify as directed by engineers.
  • Able to create library symbols/ footprint/3D drawing for component used
  • Study PCB design trends and processes and then evaluate and implement those processes that apply to Ezurio.
  • Conduct design feasibility studies to evaluate the PCB design goals for packaging, cost, manufacturing, and system performance.
  • Perform complex and difficult CAD and CAE tasks requiring extensive skill and knowledge of equipment capabilities, applications techniques and design limitations.
  • Ensure PCBs are designed to observe the principle of design for test (DFT) and design for manufacturability (DFM).
  • Propose PCB design trade-offs to the engineering design team for resolution and implementation.
  • Communicate with fabrication vendors for quotations and purchase requisitions also responsible to engineering questions (EQ) from PCB fabricators.
  • Understands the requirements for a quality design and strives to achieve the requirements before releasing the product to manufacturing.
  • Understands the impedance control requirement of the different electrical bus interfaces and RF circuits, familiar with the basic rule of thumb to achieve SI (Signal Integrity) during the routing.
  • Understands the driving of PCB technology and process trends and their application to Ezurio's designs.
  • Coordinate with Engineering, Test, Quality, and Manufacturing during the PCB design and fabrication process.
  • Resolve PCB design issues with fabrication and manufacturing vendors.
  • Participate and provide input into the PCB design specifications and standards with respect to product design, electrical design, manufacturing and various regulatory agency requirements to determine design trade-offs necessary to meet design goals and produce high quality PCB's at the lowest cost and within schedule.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Demonstrate proficient hands-on use of Altium Designer for PCB layout, library management, and PCB design release. Experience with Cadence or Mentor PCB design tools is a plus.
  • Ability of using Mechanical CAD tools like Solidwork/AutoCad is preferred.
  • Must demonstrate an ability to read schematics
  • Proficient working knowledge of PCB design best practices and applicable IPC standards, including IPC-2221, IPC-7351, IPC-A-600, and IPC-6012. Knowledge of IPC-A-610 is also preferred.
  • Demonstrated strong and effective verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelors or Technical Degree and a minimum of 5 years related experience required
  • Experience in RF Circuit PCB design is preferred

jobs.description:
Money stress is the biggest productivity killer in the workplace - My Money Matters exists to change that. We're building an app that improves employees' finances automatically every pay day - giving them financial tools that directly improve their financial health with less effort.

Every pay day is an opportunity to build better money habits. We make it easy. Employees can accelerate retirement savings with tax-efficient pension top-ups, build a safety net effortlessly with auto savings, or access their already-earned salary ahead of pay day for emergencies.

For employers, fewer employees with money worries means more focus on work. We're trusted by major organisations including the NHS, and we're growing fast.

The Customer Launch Lead leads My Money Matters' Launch team: the function responsible for taking every new employer from contract signature to a live, well-adopted account in under 30 days. The role combines hands-on ownership of our highest-value and most complex launches with managing and developing a small team of Customer Launch Managers.

This role reports into the Head of Account Management, reflecting that launch is the first chapter of the ongoing account relationship - get it right, and Account Management inherits a live, well-understood account that is ready to grow.

Key Responsibilities

Leading launches across the team

  • Hold the portfolio view of every launch in flight across the team, tracking progress against the 30-day target

  • Allocate incoming launches to Customer Launch Managers, matching complexity to experience and keeping workload balanced

  • Act as the escalation point for launches at risk, stepping in to unblock or reassign as needed

  • Own the handover from Sales at contract signature for the most complex or highest-value accounts, confirming scope, products, key contacts and launch date

  • Run kick-offs and agree launch plans for your own portfolio, alongside overseeing the team's

  • Set and track pre-launch sign-up targets across all the team's launches, directing employee communications with the employer and Marketing

  • Own the handover to Account Management for your own launches, and quality-check the team's handovers, so every live customer is passed on with a clear record of scope, stakeholders, sign-ups and next opportunities

Standards and continuous improvement

  • Maintain and evolve the team's launch playbook, templates and tools, so launches stay fast, consistent and repeatable

  • Spot patterns across launches - common blockers, slow points, what drives sign-up - and turn them into improvements the whole team uses

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on set-up friction and with Marketing on sign-up campaign materials

Cross-functional and senior stakeholder management

  • Represent the Launch team with Sales, Marketing, Product, Engineering and Account Management leadership

  • Feedback to Sales on what speeds up or slows down launch, so deals are shaped to launch well

  • Report to the Head of Account Management on launch pipeline, performance and risk

Team Leadership

  • Line-manage Customer Launch Managers (2 direct reports initially, may flex to 1), setting clear objectives tied to time-to-launch and sign-up targets

  • Run regular 1:1s, coaching conversations and performance reviews, and support career development within the team

  • Lead recruitment and onboarding as the team grows or changes

  • Balance a hands-on portfolio of launches with the time needed to manage and support the team well

  • Build a team culture of pace and ownership, where launches are delivered to a high standard with minimal day-to-day direction.

Skills & Competencies

Core Skills

  • Strong track record of delivery and coordination, running several launches or projects in parallel and hitting dates

  • Experience managing or mentoring others, ideally with direct line management experience (strong first-time managers with proven informal leadership will also be considered)

  • Pace and urgency: removes blockers rather than waiting for them to clear, and instils that mindset in others

  • Confident with payroll, data and integration requirements, and able to lead those conversations with customers and coach others to do the same

  • Campaign mindset: knows how to drive employee take-up through clear, well-timed communications

  • Communicates clearly and confidently with stakeholders at all levels, from payroll teams and HR directors to senior internal leadership

  • Comfortable balancing hands-on delivery with people management and team-level reporting

Experience & Background

  • Proven track record delivering customer onboarding, implementation or launches in a SaaS or platform business, ideally as a Customer Launch Manager or equivalent

  • Experience managing or developing team members, even informally (for example mentoring, leading a workstream, or deputising for a manager)

  • Experience driving user or employee adoption, ideally in employee benefits, payroll, HR or financial wellbeing

  • Experience with payroll data, integrations or HR systems is advantageous

  • Experience with public sector or other complex organisations is advantageous but not essential

What the Role Is Not

  • A reactive technical support role

  • A back-office set-up role: launch success is measured by sign-ups, not just go-live

  • A long-term account role: once a customer is live, the Account Manager takes over

  • A role requiring task-level direction

This role suits someone who loves pace and ownership and wants to see every launch go live quickly with employees signed up and ready to benefit.

Overview

Quality strategy and automation leadership

jobs.description:
More than 80% of Americans own a car and see it as a fundamental necessity, yet the experience of owning one is stuck in the 90s. At Jerry.ai, we are building the first app to manage it all. Since launching in 2019, we’ve reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and achieved profitability in 2024.

Jerry operates across the US and Canada, and our legal team keeps all of it running: entity filings, IP protection, compliance audits, consumer escalations, regulatory changes, and the systems behind them. The team is small, so this role comes with real scope early. You’ll own Jerry’s legal and compliance operations: make sure recurring work is done right, run the programs that need judgment, and keep rebuilding them with AI and low-code tools, so a small team can do the work of a much larger one.

The person who succeeds in this role is a natural driver: someone who owns their work from start to finish, solves complex problems without a manual, and has the grit to thrive in a startup environment. If you are eager to sit at the intersection of law, technology, and AI-driven efficiency, we want to hear from you.

Why You Will (Or Won’t) Like Working Here

  • Real ownership early: You report directly to our Legal Counsel and work closely with them across the team’s full scope. You’ll own a set of compliance programs for the long term, and you’ll be the first point of contact for teammates who run day-to-day compliance work.

  • Room to build: Many of our legal processes are still being optimized. You’ll decide how they should work and build the systems behind them.

  • Building and operating: Alongside the building, a large share of the job is recurring work: filings, deadlines, audits, complaint responses, and quality checks that have to be done exactly right, every time. Your accuracy keeps Jerry in good standing in every jurisdiction, and people who enjoy both sides of the role do well here.

  • Growth that tracks results: You’ll learn from leaders who come from Amazon, Better, LinkedIn, McKinsey, BCG, and Bain. Promotion is based on performance and ownership alone, so strong work moves you forward fast.

What You’ll Own

  • Compliance operations: Run, review, and quality-check the recurring compliance work, including entity maintenance, privacy requests, and licensing support.

  • Marketing compliance and audits: Run TCPA and Do Not Call audits, monitor opt-outs, and keep marketing guidelines current. Check the accuracy of AI-powered audits, and design new audit programs with sampling plans and scoring rubrics.

  • Consumer escalations: Investigate complex escalations to their root cause, work with Product, Operations, and Engineering on the fix, and turn recurring issues into compliance training for teams across the company.

  • Regulatory change and readiness: Track regulatory changes, along with issues surfaced by complaints and audits, and see each one through to action. Keep Jerry ready to answer regulator inquiries, carrier audits, and partner diligence quickly.

  • Legal team support: Support contract renewals, legal research, and product reviews with intake, fact gathering, trackers, and follow-up.

  • Automation and AI: Replace manual legal tasks with AI and low-code workflows, and own the reliability of every script, report, and AI tool the team depends on.

Who You Are

  • A Closer: You track every open item until it’s done, and you find the answer yourself before asking someone else for it.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). About the role

We are looking for a deeply technical Senior Retention Specialist to own the CRM build for a high-growth consumer technology client. You will architect and implement the flows and automations that carry the program, own the segmentation logic behind them, and hold the channel KPIs that determine whether any of it lands in the inbox.

You are standing this program up from the ground, not inheriting it. The list starts near 20,000 and scales rapidly behind a significant acquisition investment — which puts real pressure on deliverability, list hygiene, and data hygiene from day one. Volume ramps to 40–60 emails a month, and increasingly granular segmentation is what generates that output. Automation is the core of the program: lead capture, welcome series, and the first-conversion funnel first, then subscription activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back. You will work in an enterprise-grade platform — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

You are the person who knows the platform better than anyone else on the team. When something does not fire, does not render, or does not deliver, you find out why.

Working hours: PST (mandatory). This role includes monthly travel to San Francisco.

You should apply if this sounds like you

You are hands-on in the ESP every day and you like it there. You enjoy building a journey with real conditional logic, and you get genuine satisfaction from tracking down why one segment stopped converting.

  • 3–5+ years of hands-on lifecycle, CRM, or email marketing execution, with deep expertise in at least one enterprise-grade ESP — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

  • You have built complex, event-triggered journeys from scratch: multi-branch logic, wait steps, conditional splits, holdouts, and cross-channel orchestration across email, SMS, push, and in-app.

  • You are fluent in advanced segmentation — behavioral and product-event based, computed attributes, dynamic and personalized content — and you have scaled a program where segmentation drove a real increase in send volume.

  • You have built the funnel that matters here: lead capture forms and opt-in logic, welcome series, first-conversion sequences, and subscription activation journeys.

  • You have implemented loyalty, rewards, and win-back programs, and you treat driving repeat purchase and long-term value as a core outcome rather than a nice-to-have.

  • You own the channel KPIs — open, click, click-to-open, conversion, deliverability, bounce, spam complaints, unsubscribe — and you can diagnose a drop in any of them.

  • You are comfortable with HTML and CSS for email, and you know how to build templates and modules that render correctly across clients. Liquid, Handlebars, AMPscript, or a similar templating language is a strong plus.

  • You understand data flows into the ESP: API-based events, webhooks, ETL or CDP integrations, and product event streams. You can hold a technical conversation with a client's engineering team.

  • You are a systematic troubleshooter — you isolate variables, you check the data before the theory, and you document what you find.

  • You design and execute proper tests: A/B and multivariate, with honest reads on significance.

  • Excellent written communication and the ability to explain a technical problem to a non-technical audience clearly and without condescension.

A day in the life

We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Responsibilities

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Peraton is seeking a Senior GIS Developer to lead the production of federal species range maps for a high-priority data integration program. You will produce range maps for marine and anadromous taxa in compliance with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), facilitating iterative review cycles with government SMEs and coordinating formal government sign-off.

Work Location: Remote

Day to Day Responsibilities:

  • Lead species range map production, producing complete range maps for all marine and anadromous taxa in full compliance with the FWS Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
  • Obtain and review the FWS Range Mapping SOP at or before project kickoff

About

We are reimagining the phone. AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost. This is a mission critical for rest of the world to adopt intelligence.

There are over 5 billion people using everyday applications such as email, messaging, notes, tasks, and calendars, yet most are not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications and devices that bring intelligence into daily conversations, coordination and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Focus: Defining the hardware platform strategy and specifications for the AI-native phone, ensuring the selected hardware can support both current and future AI capabilities.

This is a more strategic hardware role than Device Integration. The focus is on evaluating hardware architectures, selecting the right SoC and components, defining device specifications, and working with ODMs to translate product requirements into hardware designs.

Responsibilities

  • Define the overall hardware platform strategy and roadmap for the phone.

  • Evaluate and compare mobile SoC platforms, including Qualcomm, MediaTek and other potential vendors.

  • Define hardware specifications covering CPU, GPU, NPU, RAM, storage, memory bandwidth and connectivity.

  • Evaluate NPU capabilities, supported AI frameworks, compute performance and memory constraints for on-device AI workloads.

  • Define hardware requirements for AI-native features, including always-on hotword detection, camera and audio processing, background AI execution and sensor integration.

  • Evaluate power consumption, thermal performance, battery capacity and sustained compute performance.

  • Work with product and AI teams to translate future AI capabilities into hardware requirements.

  • Assess whether existing commercial platforms can meet our requirements or whether deeper hardware customization is necessary.

  • Work directly with ODM/OEM and chipset vendors to review platform proposals, component selection and technical feasibility.

  • Review hardware architecture, component specifications and design trade-offs proposed by ODMs.

  • Identify opportunities for dedicated AI accelerators, low-power processing and other hardware capabilities that could differentiate the device.

  • Establish hardware validation criteria and ensure the selected platform has sufficient headroom for future software and AI capabilities.

Requirements

  • Strong experience in smartphone hardware architecture, mobile SoC or embedded hardware engineering.

  • Deep understanding of mobile SoC architecture, including CPU, GPU, NPU, memory subsystem and hardware acceleration.

  • Experience evaluating and selecting smartphone hardware platforms.

  • Understanding of power architecture, thermal management, battery performance and hardware constraints.

  • Experience defining hardware specifications and technical requirements for mobile devices.

  • Experience working directly with ODM/OEM, chipset vendors and hardware suppliers.

  • Ability to translate product and AI requirements into concrete hardware specifications and platform decisions.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Qualcomm Snapdragon or MediaTek Dimensity platforms.

  • Experience with AI accelerator / NPU architecture and on-device AI workloads.

  • Experience with smartphone hardware design and component selection.

  • Experience with camera ISP, audio DSP and sensor architecture.

  • Experience taking a smartphone product from platform selection through mass production.

  • Experience with custom hardware platforms or ODM product development.

jobs.excerpt: AboutWe are reimagining the phone.  AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost.
jobs.description:
About

We are reimagining the phone. AI phones need to be proactive, intuitive, intelligent and low cost. This is a mission critical for rest of the world to adopt intelligence.

There are over 5 billion people using everyday applications such as email, messaging, notes, tasks, and calendars, yet most are not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications and devices that bring intelligence into daily conversations, coordination and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Focus: Designing and implementing the security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone, ensuring AI agents can safely access user data, interact with applications, and execute actions across the operating system.

Unlike conventional mobile application security, this role needs to consider the additional risks introduced by AI agents having access to personal context, system services, and application-level actions.

Responsibilities

  • Design the overall security and privacy architecture for the AI-native phone.

  • Define permission models and access boundaries for AI agents interacting with user data and system services.

  • Design secure mechanisms for AI access to messages, contacts, calendars, notifications, camera, microphone, location and other sensitive information.

  • Implement appropriate sandboxing and isolation for agent execution.

  • Define authentication, authorization and access-control mechanisms for AI tools and application integrations.

  • Ensure users have control over what information AI can access and what actions it can execute.

  • Implement audit logging and user-visible activity tracking for AI access and actions.

  • Design secure storage, encryption, data retention and deletion mechanisms for personal data and memory.

  • Identify and mitigate AI-specific security risks, including prompt injection, malicious applications, data exfiltration and unauthorized tool execution.

  • Review Android permission models, privileged system access, SELinux policies and system-level security boundaries.

  • Work closely with Android/AOSP, Agent Runtime, Context & Memory and Applied ML teams to ensure security is built into the architecture rather than added later.

  • Conduct security assessments, threat modeling and penetration testing for system-level AI capabilities.

Requirements

  • Strong experience in mobile security, Android security, application security or systems security.

  • Deep understanding of Android security architecture, including application sandboxing, permissions, SELinux, Binder IPC and privileged system services.

  • Experience designing authentication, authorization and access-control systems.

  • Strong understanding of encryption, secure storage, key management and data protection.

  • Experience with security threat modeling, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.

  • Understanding of privacy-by-design principles, data minimization and user consent.

  • Ability to work across Android platform, backend and AI agent architectures.

Nice to have

jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Mission

You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast.

As a Project Manager, most of your implementations are not multi-year global programs. They are for companies that want blp running in their finance or supply chain organization within weeks, and who want somebody who knows what they are doing to take them through it. You are that person. You run the kick-off, work with them on scope and process, configure blp, coordinate the integration, take them through testing, and get them across the line at go-live.

You work in three modes, and many of our Project Managers move between them:

  • Guided onboarding for our commercial customers: you run configuration days for several customers at once, guide them while they configure, and answer the questions that come up.

  • Leading yourself on enterprise customers: you own the project end to end, including the sponsor meetings.

  • Alongside a Senior Project Manager on our largest programs, where you take a country, an entity or a workstream and own it.

Your Career Path in Project Management

This is the path most of our delivery leadership came through, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the size of the programs you have delivered, and we are explicit about what the next step requires.

  • Project Manager: You get customers live end to end, several in parallel: guided onboarding for commercial customers, leading enterprise projects yourself, or a workstream on our largest programs. Typically you bring 2+ years in consulting, implementation or project management.

  • Senior Project Manager: You make large, global transformations happen: multiple ERPs, entities and countries, the steering committee, and a blp team on each engagement. Typically you bring 5+ years delivering complex, multi-country programs.

  • Next steps: Lead a delivery team, or move into Consulting and from there towards our Client Partner role on strategic accounts.

Moves into Consulting or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run implementations end to end: kick-off, scope, planning, configuration, testing and go-live.

  • Manage several customers in parallel at different stages, and keep every one of them on date.

  • Work with customers on their processes, and flag early where a process assumption will not hold.

  • Coordinate the specialists on your projects: Integrations Engineers, Technical Project Managers and AI Automation Specialists.

  • Own scope actively. Recognize a change request for what it is and handle it deliberately.

  • Keep the project inside its budget, and raise it early when the effort is drifting.

  • Hand over cleanly at go-live to our Consultants and support organization.

In addition, as a Senior Project Manager

  • Own the delivery outcome of global programs from kick-off to the last go-live: plan, scope, dependencies and date.

  • Drive the first go-live relentlessly, then run wave planning across ERPs, entities and countries.

  • Run the steering committee and own the decisions that come out of it.

  • Write and execute the recovery plan when a program is off track.

  • Lead the blp team on each engagement and coach the Project Managers working on your programs.

What We're Really Looking For

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Scope Discipline – You notice when a project is quietly growing, and you raise it rather than absorbing it.

  • Ownership & Autonomy – You take initiative, move things forward, and deliver end to end without being chased.

  • Escalation Judgment – You escalate early, to the right person, with a proposal rather than a problem.

  • Client Confidence – You are comfortable running a meeting with a customer's finance or IT lead in it.

  • Four-Language Fluency – Technology, process, data and people. You speak each well enough to spot where a roadblock really sits.

  • Structured Under Pressure – When a project goes sideways you get sharper and more organized, not louder.

What You Bring

For the Project Manager level

  • Master's degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

  • 1+ years of experience in consulting, technical implementation, process automation, or project management.

  • The ability to run several projects at once without losing control of any of them.

  • Strong analytical and communication skills. You can translate a business need into something a technical team can act on.

  • Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

  • Bonus points for ERP implementation experience, finance or supply chain processes, or AI-driven SaaS.

Benefits

  • High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

  • Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

  • Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

  • Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

  • Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home or the office, with occasional visits to customers across the DACH region.

Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.

Your Mission

You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast.

As a Project Manager, most of your implementations are not multi-year global programs. They are for companies that want blp running in their finance or supply chain organization within weeks, and who want somebody who knows what they are doing to take them through it. You are that person. You run the kick-off, work with them on scope and process, configure blp, coordinate the integration, take them through testing, and get them across the line at go-live.

You work in three modes, and many of our Project Managers move between them:

  • Guided onboarding for our commercial customers: you run configuration days for several customers at once, guide them while they configure, and answer the questions that come up.

  • Leading yourself on enterprise customers: you own the project end to end, including the sponsor meetings.

  • Alongside a Senior Project Manager on our largest programs, where you take a country, an entity or a workstream and own it.

Your Career Path in Project Management

This is the path most of our delivery leadership came through, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the size of the programs you have delivered, and we are explicit about what the next step requires.

  • Project Manager: You get customers live end to end, several in parallel: guided onboarding for commercial customers, leading enterprise projects yourself, or a workstream on our largest programs. Typically you bring 2+ years in consulting, implementation or project management.

  • Senior Project Manager: You make large, global transformations happen: multiple ERPs, entities and countries, the steering committee, and a blp team on each engagement. Typically you bring 5+ years delivering complex, multi-country programs.

  • Next steps: Lead a delivery team, or move into Consulting and from there towards our Client Partner role on strategic accounts.

Moves into Consulting or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run implementations end to end: kick-off, scope, planning, configuration, testing and go-live.

  • Manage several customers in parallel at different stages, and keep every one of them on date.

  • Work with customers on their processes, and flag early where a process assumption will not hold.

  • Coordinate the specialists on your projects: Integrations Engineers, Technical Project Managers and AI Automation Specialists.

  • Own scope actively. Recognize a change request for what it is and handle it deliberately.

  • Keep the project inside its budget, and raise it early when the effort is drifting.

  • Hand over cleanly at go-live to our Consultants and support organization.

In addition, as a Senior Project Manager

  • Own the delivery outcome of global programs from kick-off to the last go-live: plan, scope, dependencies and date.

  • Drive the first go-live relentlessly, then run wave planning across ERPs, entities and countries.

  • Run the steering committee and own the decisions that come out of it.

  • Write and execute the recovery plan when a program is off track.

  • Lead the blp team on each engagement and coach the Project Managers working on your programs.

What We're Really Looking For

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Scope Discipline – You notice when a project is quietly growing, and you raise it rather than absorbing it.

  • Ownership & Autonomy – You take initiative, move things forward, and deliver end to end without being chased.

  • Escalation Judgment – You escalate early, to the right person, with a proposal rather than a problem.

  • Client Confidence – You are comfortable running a meeting with a customer's finance or IT lead in it.

  • Four-Language Fluency – Technology, process, data and people. You speak each well enough to spot where a roadblock really sits.

  • Structured Under Pressure – When a project goes sideways you get sharper and more organized, not louder.

What You Bring

For the Project Manager level

  • Master's degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

  • 2+ years of experience in consulting, technical implementation, process automation, or project management.

  • The ability to run several projects at once without losing control of any of them.

  • Strong analytical and communication skills. You can translate a business need into something a technical team can act on.

  • Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

  • Bonus points for ERP implementation experience, finance or supply chain processes, or AI-driven SaaS.

Benefits

  • High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

  • Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

  • Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

  • Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

  • Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Learn more about blp and our values at .
