  • Cross-functional BVA & forecast reviews: a recurring cadence with Marketing, Retail, and Ops leads, turning variance into clear drivers and next steps, not just a report-out
  • New product & channel investment modeling: build or gut-check the financial case for new launches, channel expansion, and other growth bets, partnering with cross-functional teams
  • Process & planning infrastructure: build scalable, repeatable processes that bring accuracy and speed to every planning cycle, not just this year's fire drill
  • Contribute to Board & investor reporting
  • Mentorship: help grow the team's skills and capabilities as the function matures

Requirements

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 7 to 10 years of FP&A experience, omni-channel CPG strongly preferred
  • Track record of building scalable, repeatable planning processes, not just one-off models
  • Comfortable working directly in a modern data warehouse plus a BI tool
  • Genuine fluency using AI tools to accelerate analysis and modeling
  • Experience mentoring and developing team members
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication, comfortable presenting to leadership

NICE TO HAVE

Benefits

The actual salary offer will take into account multiple factors including skills, experience, education and location. Please note that the salary details listed in role postings reflect the base salary only, not total compensation, which includes equity and benefits.

Everyday Dose offers comprehensive medical, vision, dental, and prescription plan coverage for all team members working 32+ hours per week. Eligibility begins on the first of the month following your start date, and we cover 75% of employee premiums.

401K Match

Starting on the first day of your fourth month with the company, you are eligible to participate in our company-sponsored 401(k) plan. The company offers a match of up to 80% of your contributions, capped at 5% of your salary.

The ideal candidate is an empathetic and proactive self-starter with a team-lead mentality; someone who works directly with customers, owns issues end to end, and sets the technical standard for the team through mentorship, enablement, and example. This role also serves as a trusted technical voice to Product Management and executive leadership, translating field and customer insights into product and business decisions.

  • Provide hybrid pre-sales and post-sales engineering support, including technical discovery, solution design, demonstrations, proofs of concept, onboarding, deployment guidance, escalation management, and issue resolution through closure

  • Own the technical customer onboarding experience for assigned accounts, accelerating time to value and protecting revenue recognition and customer satisfaction

  • Partner directly with CIS Services Account Executives and Senior Account Executives throughout the government sales cycle, including procurement, security reviews, and technical evaluations

  • Proactively engage customers and internal stakeholders through direct, real-time communication (phone, video, and possibly, in-person meetings) to accelerate resolution and build trusted relationships

  • Act as a technical team lead and mentor; coaching, enabling, and upskilling solutions engineers whose experience is concentrated in CIS SecureSuite, broadening team competency across the managed security services portfolio

  • Develop enablement content, runbooks, demonstration environments, and best-practice documentation that matures team capability and shortens team ramp time

  • Deliver professional presentations and technical demonstrations via phone, web technologies, and live and virtual conferences, articulating the value of foundational cybersecurity as the core of all organizational initiatives

  • Serve as the voice of the customer; synthesize field feedback to inform Product Management priorities and support executive decision-making, collaborating regularly with product managers, Security Operations, and Engineering

  • Identify cross-sell and upgrade opportunities; assist sales through deal closure and build use case recommendations, case studies, and testimonials

  • Track all account contact, opportunities, and support activity in Salesforce, ensuring reporting and communication is frequent and bi-directional

  • Represent CIS in a general capacity and present at conferences or product meetings as necessary

  • Other tasks and responsibilities as assigned

What You'll Need:

  • Bachelor's degree in technical or business discipline*

  • 5+ years of sales engineering, solutions engineering, or technical account management experience in cybersecurity, with demonstrated pre-sales and post-sales responsibilities

  • Deep knowledge of managed security services, including MDR, EDR/XDR/MXDR, NDR/IDS, and DNS-layer security; direct experience with CrowdStrike Falcon and/or Sophos platforms

  • Strong network engineering fundamentals (TCP/IP, routing, firewalls, network sensor/IDS deployment) and working knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including hardened/secured image concepts

  • Understanding of U.S. SLTT government environments, procurement, and public-sector sales cycles

  • Demonstrated experience mentoring, training, or technically leading other engineers

  • Proactive, customer-first communication style with a proven willingness to engage by phone and drive issues to full resolution across pre-sales, onboarding, and post-sales

  • Strong presentation and communication skills, both verbal and written, including technical remote demonstrations via Microsoft Teams or real-time applications

  • Familiarity with Salesforce and Microsoft Office

  • Ability to work independently and with the team collaboratively in a fast-paced environment

  • Ability to travel as needed

  • Must be authorized to work in the United States

It's a Plus if You Have:

  • Experience supporting or working within U.S. SLTT agencies, nonprofits, or Multi-State and Election Infrastructure Information Sharing and Analysis Center (MS-ISAC/EI-ISAC) member organizations

  • Related security and technical certifications (e.g., Security+, CISSP, GIAC, CrowdStrike CCFA/CCFH, Sophos certifications, cloud certifications)

jobs.description:
Software Engineering Intern

Are you currently a college student looking to start your career in software engineering? Do you want hands-on experience working with real production systems while learning from experienced engineers? Nucleus Security is seeking a Software Engineering Intern with an interest in full stack development to join our Engineering organization.

Location

AUS Remote

Department

Engineering

Employment Type

Internship (Paid)
Due to business and regulatory requirements, we are only able to hire Australian citizens at this time.

About Nucleus Security

Nucleus Security helps organizations manage and prioritize vulnerabilities at scale by unifying data from scanners, cloud platforms, and other security tools. Our platform ingests, normalizes, and acts on large volumes of security data to help customers improve their security posture efficiently.

Role Overview

As a Software Engineering Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers to contribute to systems that support integrations, workflows, APIs, and internal tooling across the Nucleus platform. This internship is designed for students who are still in college and intend to begin their careers in software engineering.

You will contribute to real code used by production systems while working on carefully scoped projects that prioritize learning, code quality, and maintainability. No prior professional software engineering experience is required.

What You’ll Work On

Depending on team needs and your interests, you may:
  1. Leverage AI to build new features and fix bugs in a Cyber Security Vulnerability Management Platform
  2. Build out new components for our ReactJS frontend.
  3. Work with third party REST APIs to build new ETL integrations.
  4. Write and improve automated tests to increase reliability and confidence.
  5. Debug issues and learn how to diagnose problems in distributed systems.
  6. Collaborate in code reviews and technical discussions with your team.

Required Qualifications

  1. Have previous internship, co-op, or equivalent experience in software engineering or a related field.
  2. Be currently enrolled in a college or university program with plans to graduate on or before June 2027.
  3. Be pursuing a degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related field.
  4. Be interested in starting a career in software engineering.
  5. Be willing to learn, ask questions, and receive feedback.
  6. Due to business and regulatory requirements, we are only able to hire Australian citizens at this time.

Nice to Have (Not Required)

  1. Experience with PHP and modern PHP practices.
  2. Experience with Python and modern Python practices.
  3. Experience with React and Typescript.
  4. Experience with relational databases such as MySQL.
  5. Familiarity with REST APIs, JSON, and HTTP.
  6. Experience writing or debugging unit tests.
  7. Basic familiarity with Git, Linux, or CI/CD concepts.
  8. Experience working in an Agile development environment.
  9. Interest in cybersecurity, integrations, or developer tooling.

Internship Experience & Outcomes

Throughout the internship, you will work on one or more well-scoped projects under the guidance of a mentor. At the conclusion of the internship, you will present to the engineering team what you worked on, the problems you tackled, and what you learned.

Why Nucleus?

  • At Nucleus Security, you will:
Gain hands-on experience working on real-world software systems.
Learn professional engineering practices in a supportive, mentorship-driven environment.
Collaborate with a high-performing, distributed engineering team.
Work remotely with flexibility and a strong emphasis on learning and growth.
Nucleus Security is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability.

jobs.description:
About Concept Plus

Concept Plus is a mission-focused technology solutions provider that transforms IT concepts into impactful solutions for federal agencies. Headquartered in Fairfax, VA, we bring the agility, responsiveness, and customer intimacy of a small business combined with the quality and infrastructure of a larger firm.

Recognized as an award-winning Oracle partner, we have delivered innovative solutions across Defense, Intelligence, Civilian, Health IT, and Tribal sectors. Our highly certified experts build systems that drive efficiency, accelerate modernization, and ensure mission outcomes with certainty.

We offer competitive pay, comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance, paid life insurance, paid time off, 11 paid holidays, performance bonuses, tuition reimbursement, unlimited training, and the opportunity to thrive in a collaborative, flexible, and innovative environment.

For more information, visit .

About the role

Concept Plus is seeking an Okta ICAM Engineer to support client ICAM modernization initiatives. This role focuses on integrating and optimizing identity solutions within environments that utilize client credentials, federation services, and Zero Trust architecture aligned with federal standards, including NIST SP 800 63, OMB ICAM guidelines, and client identity directives.

What you'll do

  • Design, implement, and maintain ICAM solutions using Okta Identity Cloud in support of federal identity requirements, including Workforce Identity, SSO, MFA, and adaptive authentication.
  • Integrate Okta with client credential systems, including certificate-based authentication, PKI validation, and federation with government identity providers.
  • Configure and support identity federation using SAML, OIDC, and OAuth across government applications, platforms, and on-prem enterprise systems.
  • Develop and manage identity lifecycle processes aligned with federal access control policies, RBAC/ABAC models, and authoritative identity sources.
  • Implement Zero Trust identity pillars, including strong authentication, device trust, continuous validation, and least-privilege access principles.
  • Build automation and identity workflows using Okta Workflows, APIs, and scripting tools to support compliance and operational efficiency.
  • Troubleshoot identity-related issues across client authentication flows, PKI chains, SSO integrations, and SCIM provisioning.
  • Ensure compliance with NIST 800 63, FICAM architecture standards, DoD IdAM policies, and FedRAMP security controls where required.
  • Collaborate closely with cybersecurity, cloud engineering, and system owners to support secure identity integration for mission systems.
  • Contribute to ICAM modernization roadmaps, ATO support documentation, and continuous improvements in identity posture..

Required Qualifications

  • US Citizen
  • 5–8+ years of experience in ICAM/IAM engineering within federal or government environments.
  • 3–5+ years of hands-on experience with Okta Identity Cloud (administration, integration, federation).
  • Practical experience supporting PIV/CAC-based authentication, PKI trust chains, certificate mapping, and federation with federal IdPs.
  • Strong understanding of authentication protocols (SAML, OIDC, OAuth), SCIM provisioning, and directory services (Active Directory, Azure AD).
  • Experience with identity policy, RBAC/ABAC, account lifecycle management, and enterprise identity governance.
  • Hands-on experience with automation (PowerShell, Python, or Bash).
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust identity architecture, especially in federal or DoD environments.
  • Excellent documentation, communication, and collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting ICAM modernization initiatives in federal agencies or DoW environments.
  • Okta Professional or Consultant Certification.
  • Familiarity with NIST SP 800 63, NIST CSF, OMB ICAM guidance, DoD Zero Trust Strategy, and FedRAMP controls.
  • Experience integrating identity services with Azure Government, or on-prem mission systems.

Concept Plus is an Equal Opportunity Employer. As such, we will give your application full consideration without regard to your race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.description:
WE ARE HIRING: Data Protection Officer

Location: Sri Lanka
Employment Type: Full-time
Company Industry: Financial Services / Banking & Regulated Institutions

Role Overview

We are looking for a Data Protection Officer to lead and manage the organizations enterprise-wide data protection and privacy program. This role is responsible for ensuring compliance with applicable data protection laws, regulatory requirements, and international information security standards while embedding privacy and security controls across business and technology operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement, and maintain the enterprise data protection and privacy program.

  • Ensure compliance with PDPA, Central Bank of Sri Lanka regulations, and internal governance frameworks.

  • Work closely with IT and Cybersecurity teams to embed privacy-by-design principles and security controls.

  • Conduct privacy impact assessments and data protection risk assessments, and drive corrective actions.

  • Lead ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27701 implementation and ongoing compliance initiatives.

  • Establish and maintain data protection policies, procedures, and awareness programs.

  • Liaise with the Data Protection Authority and support audits and regulatory reporting requirements.

Qualifications & Experience

Educational Qualifications

jobs.excerpt: Recruiter / Talent Acquisition Specialist – Full-Cycle Recruiting | RemotePosition Type: Full-Time, Remote Working Hours: U.
jobs.description:
Recruiter / Talent Acquisition Specialist – Full-Cycle Recruiting | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Recruiter / Talent Acquisition Specialist to own the full recruiting lifecycle — from sourcing and screening candidates through interviews, offers, and successful hires.

This is a hands-on, execution-focused recruiting role for someone who knows how to build strong candidate pipelines, proactively source talent, assess candidates effectively, and keep multiple hiring processes moving simultaneously.

You’ll work closely with hiring managers and clients across different industries, helping them identify and secure high-quality talent while delivering a professional and responsive candidate experience.

If you enjoy sourcing, interviewing, and turning hiring requirements into successful placements, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

Full-Cycle Recruiting

  • Manage hiring processes from initial intake through offer acceptance
  • Partner with hiring managers to understand:
    • Role requirements
    • Ideal candidate profiles
    • Hiring priorities
    • Compensation expectations
    • Hiring timelines
  • Create and optimize job descriptions to attract relevant candidates
  • Maintain momentum across multiple open positions simultaneously
  • Keep hiring processes organized and moving toward successful placements

Candidate Sourcing & Pipeline Development

  • Source active and passive candidates through:
    • LinkedIn Recruiter
    • Indeed
    • Glassdoor
    • Boolean search
    • Niche job boards
  • Build targeted candidate pipelines based on hiring requirements
  • Conduct proactive outreach to qualified candidates
  • Go beyond inbound applicants to identify passive talent
  • Develop reusable talent pools for recurring hiring needs
  • Evaluate sourcing channels based on candidate quality and conversion

Screening & Interviewing

  • Conduct structured phone and video interviews
  • Assess candidates based on:
    • Relevant experience
    • Communication skills
    • Technical or functional fit
    • Career goals
    • Role alignment
    • Culture and working-style fit
  • Administer assessments or screening exercises when required
  • Prepare clear candidate summaries and hiring recommendations
  • Maintain detailed and accurate interview notes in the ATS

Candidate Experience

  • Keep candidates informed throughout every stage of the hiring process
  • Coordinate interviews across multiple schedules and time zones
  • Prepare candidates for client and hiring manager interviews
  • Manage candidate follow-ups promptly
  • Communicate expectations and next steps clearly
  • Deliver a professional, responsive, and organized candidate experience

Hiring Manager & Client Partnership

  • Provide regular updates on pipeline health and hiring progress
  • Share relevant market feedback regarding:
    • Candidate availability
    • Compensation
    • Hiring challenges
    • Talent quality
  • Facilitate interview debriefs and hiring discussions
  • Help hiring managers make informed decisions through structured candidate evaluations
  • Build trusted relationships with clients and internal stakeholders

Offer Management & Hiring Support

  • Prepare and present candidate offers
  • Support compensation discussions and negotiations
  • Address candidate questions during the offer stage
  • Maintain consistent communication to help reduce offer drop-off
  • Coordinate hiring documentation and onboarding handoffs

Recruiting Operations & Reporting

  • Maintain clean and accurate ATS records
  • Track recruiting metrics including:
    • Time-to-fill
    • Source effectiveness
    • Pipeline health
    • Interview conversion rates
    • Offer acceptance
  • Maintain recruiting dashboards and hiring reports
  • Ensure candidates move through pipeline stages accurately and efficiently

Requirements

  • 2+ years of recruiting, talent acquisition, or staffing experience
  • Experience managing multiple open positions simultaneously
  • Strong hands-on sourcing experience using LinkedIn Recruiter
  • Strong Boolean search skills
  • Experience conducting structured candidate interviews
  • Experience with ATS platforms such as:
    • Greenhouse
    • Lever
    • JazzHR
    • iCIMS
    • Similar recruiting systems
  • Strong candidate assessment and evaluation skills
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication
  • Strong organizational and pipeline-management skills
  • High attention to detail and consistent follow-through
  • Ability to work effectively during U.S. client business hours

Nice to Have

  • Agency recruiting or staffing experience
  • High-volume recruiting background
  • Experience recruiting across:
    • SaaS
    • Technology
    • Finance
    • Property Management
    • Professional Services
  • Experience recruiting across multiple job functions simultaneously
  • Knowledge of recruiting analytics and hiring metrics
  • Familiarity with employment law and hiring compliance

Tools & Platforms

LinkedIn Recruiter | Indeed | Glassdoor | Greenhouse | Lever | JazzHR | iCIMS | Boolean Search | ATS Platforms | Recruiting & Sourcing Tools

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

  • Genuinely enjoy finding and engaging strong candidates
  • Know how to go beyond job-board applicants and proactively source talent
  • Can quickly determine whether someone is genuinely qualified
  • Balance hiring speed with candidate quality
  • Stay organized while managing several open roles and candidate pipelines
  • Communicate confidently with candidates, clients, and hiring managers
  • Follow up consistently without needing reminders
  • Treat candidate experience as an important part of successful recruiting
  • Take ownership of searches from intake through successful hire

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day may include sourcing candidates through LinkedIn and job boards, running Boolean searches for difficult-to-fill roles, and reaching out to passive candidates.

You’ll conduct recruiter screens, prepare candidate summaries and recommendations, coordinate client interviews, follow up with candidates and hiring managers, and keep ATS stages and interview notes current.

You may also review pipeline health, evaluate sourcing performance, and support offers and negotiations.

In short: you build strong candidate pipelines and manage the recruiting process from initial search through successful hire.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Time-to-fill
  • Candidate quality
  • Interview pass-through rates
  • Sourcing effectiveness
  • Pipeline health
  • Offer acceptance rates
  • Candidate responsiveness and experience
  • Hiring manager satisfaction
  • ATS accuracy and recruiting compliance

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Full ownership across the recruiting lifecycle
  • Opportunity to recruit across multiple industries and job functions
  • Direct interaction with hiring managers and clients
  • Strong exposure to sourcing, interviewing, and talent strategy
  • Fast-paced environment with measurable hiring impact
  • Career growth opportunities into:
    • Senior Recruiter
    • Talent Acquisition Partner
    • Recruiting Lead
    • Recruitment Manager

Interview Process

  1. Initial Application
  2. Spark Hire One-Way Video Interview
  3. Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  4. Practical Recruiting Task – Boolean Search & Candidate Sourcing Exercise
  5. Client Interview
  6. Offer & Background Verification

Spark Hire Video Interview – Required

As part of the application process, all candidates are required to complete a one-way video interview through Spark Hire.

After completing the first step of your application, you’ll receive a Spark Hire invitation by email with instructions to record and submit your video responses.

Completion of the Spark Hire video is required to be considered for the next stage. Please check your inbox as well as your spam or junk folder for the invitation.

Apply Now

If you have full-cycle recruiting experience, enjoy proactively sourcing and identifying high-quality talent, and can manage fast-moving hiring pipelines without sacrificing candidate experience, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and take ownership of hiring across multiple roles while continuing to grow your career in talent acquisition and recruitment.

jobs.title: Strategic Customer Success Manager, Australia & New Zealand
jobs.excerpt: Shape Customer Success in a higher education market with momentum.
jobs.description:
Shape Customer Success in a higher education market with momentum.

Some Customer Success roles ask you to step into a well-established portfolio and follow a proven playbook.

This one gives you more room to shape what comes next.

You’ll take ownership of a growing portfolio of university partners across Australia and New Zealand, helping them get meaningful value from Acuity’s products, data, research, and insights.

That includes Casper, our established situational judgment assessment used by higher education institutions around the world, alongside newer products and capabilities we’re beginning to bring to market. As our portfolio grows, you’ll help partners understand what’s possible, connect their needs to the right solutions, and identify where those partnerships can deepen over time.

You’ll also have the opportunity to extend your impact beyond your customer portfolio, helping build our regional presence while growing the business already there.

You’ll spend time with partners in person. Build relationships across institutions and the broader higher education community. Represent Acuity at conferences and industry events. Bring local insight and perspective into a Canadian-founded company growing internationally. And help shape how we support and grow a market that already has strong momentum, but is still early in its potential.

This is a role for someone who likes to think strategically and stay close to the work. Someone who can build credibility with senior stakeholders, spot opportunities in relationships, and create momentum without waiting for a perfectly established playbook.

If you know the Australian higher education landscape, enjoy the autonomy of owning your work, and want the chance to leave a visible mark on how a market develops, this could be a particularly interesting next chapter.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based in Australia, with regular travel to meet customers and participate in industry events across the region.

Before you apply: Thoughtful use of AI is encouraged. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out.

The Work You’ll Do

At the heart of this role is owning and growing strong, strategic customer relationships across Australia and New Zealand.

You’ll:

  • Own a portfolio of university partners, building trusted relationships from day-to-day contacts to senior decision-makers and developing a deep understanding of their goals, challenges, stakeholders, and what success looks like for them.
  • Help partners get meaningful, lasting value from Acuity, using customer insight, data, and your understanding of their context to guide conversations and recommend the right path forward.
  • Stay ahead of what your customers need, identifying risks early, navigating challenges thoughtfully, and bringing the right people from across Acuity together when needed.
  • Spot opportunities to deepen and grow partnerships through greater adoption, new use cases, additional products, referrals, or connections elsewhere within an institution.
  • Work closely with our Growth team to develop opportunities across the region, bringing your customer relationships and local market knowledge into how we grow.
  • Spend meaningful time in the market, meeting partners in person, visiting campuses, and representing Acuity at conferences and industry events.
  • Bring what you’re learning back into Acuity, sharing customer and market insight that helps us better support our partners and make smarter decisions about the region.

What You’ll Help Make Possible

Partnerships that deepen over time.
Our strongest customer relationships go beyond successful adoption. They’re built on trust, shared understanding, and meaningful outcomes. You’ll help create the conditions for those partnerships to last, deepen, and open new possibilities over time.

Growth built on trust.
Some of our strongest growth in the region has come through advocacy, referrals, and word of mouth. You’ll help turn great customer relationships into greater adoption, new use cases, introductions across institutions, and opportunities to support more of the higher education community.

A stronger local presence.
Having someone on the ground changes what’s possible. Partners can see and spend time with us more easily, Acuity can participate more actively in the higher education community, and our investment in the region becomes increasingly visible.

Acuity getting smarter about the region.
Being close to the market means seeing things others might miss: what partners are talking about, how institutions are changing, where new needs are emerging, and the important differences between Australia and New Zealand. Your perspective will help shape how we support customers, evolve our approach, and decide where to invest.

Strong partnerships creating new possibilities.
By helping partners get more value from Acuity, deepening relationships across their institutions, and understanding where their needs are evolving, you’ll help create opportunities for those partnerships to grow over time.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, we’d hope to see:

Partners who trust you and value your perspective. You understand their world, know the people who matter, and have built relationships that go beyond regular check-ins. Customers see you as someone who can help them think through challenges, opportunities, and what comes next.

A healthy, growing portfolio. Your customers are realising meaningful value, risks are surfaced and addressed early, and you’re creating the conditions for strong retention, deeper adoption, and expansion over time.

A meaningful presence in the region. You’ve met our partners in person, built connections across the higher education community, and become a familiar and credible face for Acuity in Australia and New Zealand.

Growth emerging from strong relationships. You’re spotting opportunities within and beyond your portfolio, generating introductions and referrals, and working with the Go-To-Market team to turn the right opportunities into something more.

A stronger foundation for what comes next. You’re bringing useful market insight back into Acuity, advocating for what the region needs, and helping us learn what works so we can make better decisions about how we support customers and grow our presence over time.

How You’ll Work Across Acuity

You’ll be part of our Customer Success team, reporting to our Senior Manager, Customer Success and working alongside CSMs who support university partners across Acuity.

You’ll partner closely with our Go-To-Market team as you identify opportunities within existing relationships, develop referrals and new connections, and help turn regional insight into new business. You’ll also work across Product, Research, Marketing, Support, and other teams to bring the right expertise and resources to our partners when they need it.

Because you’ll be based in Australia while many of your colleagues are in Canada and Europe, you’ll often be the person closest to what’s happening in the market. We’ll rely on you not just to share what you’re seeing, but to advocate for what your customers and the region need.

That could mean bringing a Research expert into an important customer conversation, making the case for locally relevant Marketing support, connecting Product to an emerging customer need, or asking Growth to lean into an opportunity you’re seeing.

You won’t be expected to have every answer or do everything yourself. There’s plenty of expertise to draw on across Acuity. But you’ll need to be proactive and persistent about accessing it: ask questions, make clear asks, follow up, and keep the right things moving even when the people or resources you need are on the other side of the world.

Part of your role will be connecting those worlds: bringing local context into Acuity, bringing Acuity’s expertise to the region, and making sure Australia and New Zealand have a strong voice as our presence there grows.

What You’ll Bring

Success in this role is as much about how you operate as what you know. You’ll bring the judgment, curiosity, relationship skills, and ownership we look for in great Customer Success, along with the resourcefulness and resilience to help build our presence in the region.

You’re likely to thrive here if you:

  • Build trusted, strategic customer relationships. You have several years of Customer Success, Account Management, or similar experience owning complex, long-term customer relationships, and know how to build credibility across an institution, from day-to-day partners to senior decision-makers.
  • Own the health and commercial success of your portfolio. You’ve been accountable for customer outcomes, adoption, retention, and renewals, know how to identify and address risk early, and understand what it takes to keep a portfolio healthy over time.
  • See growth as part of great Customer Success. You’re commercially minded and have experience growing existing accounts through deeper adoption, new products or use cases, referrals, or expansion elsewhere within an organisation. You can recognise and develop an opportunity without turning every customer conversation into a sales conversation.
  • Know the Australian higher education landscape. You’ve worked with Australian higher education institutions and understand how universities operate, including their decision-making structures, stakeholder networks, admissions cycles, and the rhythms and nuances of the sector.
  • Operate independently without operating in isolation. You’re comfortable using your judgment, making decisions, and moving work forward autonomously, while knowing when to seek input, challenge your thinking, or bring others into the conversation.
  • Are persistent and resourceful. You ask for what you need, follow up when something matters, find another path when the first one doesn’t work, and keep momentum through ambiguity, setbacks, or competing priorities.
  • Work effectively across teams and boundaries. You know how to bring people together to solve customer problems and move opportunities forward, even when you don’t directly own the people or resources you need.
  • Stay curious and adaptable. You ask good questions, learn quickly, connect ideas across different institutions and customer needs, and adjust your approach as you learn.

Experience with admissions, assessment, education technology, health sciences, or the systems and organisations that support Australian higher education would be particularly valuable, but isn’t essential.

How We Support You

Our Australian team members are employed through our Employer of Record, Deel, with access to Acuity benefits and programs alongside Australian employment entitlements.

Transparent compensation. A base salary of $115,000–$126,000 AUD, plus a $10,000 AUD annual retention bonus and additional incentives when customer referrals lead to new business. A 12% employer superannuation contribution is provided through Deel.

Learning that grows with you. $3,000 AUD annually for professional and personal development.

Shared success. Eligibility to participate in Acuity Insights’ Employee Share Option Plan, with grants based on role and level.

Time to rest and reset. In addition to your annual leave entitlement, there’s flexibility to take additional time off when you need it, plus monthly Acuity Days and a two-week company-wide closure each December.

Health and wellbeing. Access to private health insurance or an allowance to support mental health and wellbeing. Specific availability and terms will be confirmed during the offer and Deel onboarding process.

Remote-first work. Work remotely from Australia, with company-provided tools and hardware and up to $150 AUD per month toward a co-working space where needed.

A note on working across time zones

Acuity is a Canadian-founded, remote-first company, with many of your colleagues based in North America and Europe. Some flexibility to start earlier or finish later on occasion will create overlap for team meetings and collaboration, and we’ll be thoughtful about making that sustainable.

What Happens After You Apply

We review every application carefully and don’t use AI to evaluate candidates. Our interviews are two-way conversations designed to help us understand your experience and goals, while giving you plenty of opportunity to understand the role, team, and Acuity.

Our process typically takes 2–4 weeks and includes an intro conversation with Talent, a conversation with the hiring manager, and conversations with future collaborators across Customer Success and Go-To-Market. If it’s a match, we’ll move to reference checks and a formal offer.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 140+ people, built around trust, autonomy, flexibility, and a sustainable pace. We work thoughtfully across a distributed team, creating space for deep work alongside intentional connection.

Acuity Insights has been named one of Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers for the second consecutive year, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where people can do meaningful work and grow over time.

About Acuity Insights

Acuity Insights builds products that help higher education institutions make better decisions about people, from admissions through to development.

Our work is grounded in a simple idea: people are more than their grades, and potential can be understood and developed, not just measured. Our Casper situational judgment assessment has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is backed by nearly 20 years of research.

Today, we’re evolving our products to better connect assessment, insight, and development, helping institutions identify potential and support its growth over time.

jobs.title: Research Associate - Data Curation
jobs.excerpt: Are you fascinated by the way science impacts society and do you love diving deep into the scientific literature?
jobs.description:
Are you fascinated by the way science impacts society and do you love diving deep into the scientific literature? Do you enjoy curating data and extracting insights to help advance science? If you are a curious and rigorous data enthusiast, and want to help drug discovery scientists be more effective in creating new medicines, we want to hear from you!

Drug Hunter™ () is an essential scientific intelligence platform for R&D innovators turning molecules into medicines. The Drug Hunter team distills the research behind emerging drugs and technologies into concise, but scientifically rich, searchable articles and interactive features. Drug Hunter customers include many of the world’s leading innovative biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, as well as top-tier investors.

We are seeking a rigorous data curator to join the Drug Hunter team to cover emerging drug discovery patents and other disclosures. For example, you will be responsible for triaging and curating data from scientific papers and patents, including interpreting chemical structures and biological data to surface the most important insights for our readers. The successful candidate will exhibit a high level of drug discovery scientific knowledge, with strong attention to detail and a keen focus on accuracy. An ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data is a must, as is experience reading the primary scientific and patent literature.

This role reports to a Scientific Director and is a full time , fully remote position for candidates based in North America.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct in-depth research, curation, and interpretation of scientific data from the drug discovery-related scientific and patent literature
  • Maintain high levels of rigor and accuracy in data curation and analysis, as well as the construction of databases
  • Interpretation of chemical structures and biological data
  • Contribute to data research and curation across a range of projects
  • Maintain familiarity with the biopharmaceutical industry, including an understanding of the R&D process from target discovery to commercialization, and key players in the drug discovery and development ecosystem
  • Contribute to a positive culture within the Scientific and Data teams aligned with the mission and values of the company; prioritizing facts, community, clarity, helpfulness, teamwork, and accountability

Additional Duties

  • Perform other related tasks as necessary to support the ongoing needs of Drug Hunter’s Scientific and Data teams, and associated functions

Requirements

Qualifications

  • Authorization to work in the employee’s location. Drug Hunter cannot provide US visa/Green Card sponsorship or related support relevant to the employee’s location.
  • Strong track record of data curation, with an understanding of the patent processes and patent databases
  • Ability to interpret chemical structures and biological data, as well as a familiarity with ChemDraw or similar chemical drawing software
  • Experience using spreadsheets, such as Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc
  • Familiarity with scientific databases and chemoinformatics resources, such as PubChem, PubMed,, ChEMBL, SureChEMBL, etc.
  • Basic understanding of regulatory agencies and their databases (e.g., the FDA)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities with both technical and non-technical audiences, including fluency in English
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, collaborative, start-up environment, working with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines, and tackling novel challenges
  • Digitally native, comfortable with social media, software, and new technologies and platforms, and eager to apply new best practices to a growing organization
  • Demonstrated ability to pick up new fields of expertise quickly and work with agility in a growth environment
  • Candidates with a basic understanding of Python for data processing and automation will be preferred

Education and Experience

  • A B.S. or M.S. (or equivalent) in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or chemical biology
  • 0-3 years of experience focused on data curation; preference is given to candidates with experience from biotechnology or pharmaceutical companies

Benefits

Drug Hunter provides industry-leading benefits, including the following:

  • Competitive salary, variable compensation, and equity
  • Broad range of medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees and their dependents, including generous coverage for a platinum PPO healthcare plan
  • Short-term disability and long-term disability insurance
  • Cancer and critical illness coverage
  • Up to 14 weeks paid parental leave (after 1 yr tenure) and childcare FSA plan
  • 401(k) + employer match
  • Home office set up stipend for fully remote employees
  • Learning and development support
  • Generous and flexible vacation and leave policies

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.excerpt: Interchecks Interchecks Technologies is a leading venture-backed fintech company dedicated to transforming financial transaction management.
jobs.description:
Interchecks

Interchecks Technologies is a leading venture-backed fintech company dedicated to transforming financial transaction management. We provide payment processing solutions to top operators in online sports betting and fintech.

Founded in 2016 on the simple idea that sending money should be easy, fast, and affordable, Interchecks saw businesses struggling with increasingly complex payments and consumers disappointed with their options. We decided there had to be a better way — so we built it.

Starting with 1099 vendor payments, we expanded rapidly to support real-time payments for gaming operators with the legalization of online gaming in 2018. Unlike many narrow and inflexible payout solutions, Interchecks offers a comprehensive and flexible platform with strong compliance capabilities, enabling us to serve regulated industries like gaming and replicate this success across other fintech verticals.

The Opportunity

As a Data Scientist, you will support the development of analytical models that help improve our product quality, risk outcomes, and inform business decisions. Working closely with data scientists, product managers, data engineers and data analysts, you will apply statistical methods and machine learning techniques to analyze data, uncover insights, and contribute to data-driven product improvements.

This role is ideal for someone early in their data science career who is eager to expand their technical skills while gaining experience in a product-focused environment.

The Change Business Partner will lead the people-side implementation of strategic transformation across manufacturing operations. The role requires a strong understanding of manufacturing, ERP (notably Microsoft D365), and change facilitation to support both people and site-level transitions.

  • Partner with finance, operations, and systems teams to make sure costing methods are understood, applied consistently, and support effective cost control.
  • Help operational leaders move from legacy costing approaches to standardised cost models, explaining the impact on reporting, performance measurement, and profitability.
  • Work with local teams to build understanding of how standard costs are created and maintained, including bill of materials (BOM) accuracy, labour and machine rates, and overhead allocation.
  • Deliver training and capability-building activities that strengthen cost awareness and accountability across production and planning teams.

  • Support the accuracy and integrity of costing data by identifying gaps in processes, systems, and reporting, and helping teams put the right controls in place.
  • Drive adoption of new ways of working, making sure standard costing becomes embedded in decision-making rather than simply a finance exercise.

Qualifications

  • Experience delivering change management within an industrial or manufacturing environment.
  • Understands and leads for the to-be processes and ways of working.
  • Understanding and advocating good practices in principle and in detail for a range of topics especially standard costing (cost build-up, cost drivers, variance analysis, cost updates) and margin management, but also MRP, planning, and warehousing.
  • Experience supporting or deploying standard costing frameworks within ERP systems (especially Microsoft D365), including training, data validation, and cost centre alignment.
  • Ability to engage both finance and non-finance teams in understanding the operational impact of cost changes, cost performance, and product profitability.
  • Proven ability to build relationships and influence frontline teams, middle management, and senior leaders.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills, particularly in operational and technical contexts.
  • Experience with ERP systems (JD Edwards, Microsoft D365) is a strong advantage.
  • Comfortable working at different levels of the organisation.
  • Flexible to adapt to the changing business needs of the projects.
  • Serves as best practice/quality resource within Standard costing and ERP Transformations.

Qualifications and Behaviours:

  • Aptitude to learn and adapt, seeing change opportunities and encouraging others to seek positive change.
  • Change Management or Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) is an advantage.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in finance management or transformation, or multi-site general management roles within manufacturing or industrial sectors.

We are a purpose driven organisation. Our purpose is to use advanced materials to make the world more sustainable and to improve the quality of life. We deliver on that purpose through the products that we make, and the way that we make them.

We help our customers push the limits of their processes and products to meet the demanding requirements they face, from higher process temperatures to higher product performance to increasing miniaturisation.

Job Title: Senior Manager Quality Compliance (Rare Disease)

Job Location: Washington D.C., District of Columbia, United States

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Quality Compliance Senior Manager

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world.

  • Serve as a GCP Subject Matter Expert, providing independent and objective quality advice in support of clinical trial activities and in line with current best practice.

  • Provide quality oversight for Amgen programs for all stages of products in clinical development.

  • Plan, conduct and report out on risk-based GCP audits (investigator site audits, affiliate audits, service provider audits, and study level audits) or support outsourced audits.

  • Manage/support regulatory inspections and provide guidance and feedback on responses to health authorities, including root cause and CAPA plans.

  • Provide quality oversight for the Risk Assessment Categorization Tool (RACT) for each trial to ensure the proper identification, prioritization, and mitigation of risks to critical data and processes and patient safety, welfare, and rights.

  • Support monthly meetings with clinical program level leaders to review quality and compliance related risks, including but not limited to: on-going quality issues/deviations, quality trends, program filing timelines, potential inspections, and risks related to other programs.

  • Support response generation for audit findings and self-reported deviations.

  • Support the establishment of regional expertise to ensure quality and compliance with local regulations.

  • Conduct new vendor qualifications/evaluations in a risk-based manner.

  • Prepare, analyze, and Identify data quality indicators/trends, identify areas of weakness/gaps, recommend and implement corrective actions and communicate quality metrics and other significant quality information on periodic basis to key stakeholders.

  • Support TA-specific oversight of key technologies, including technologies for endpoint data collection and measurement (e.g., biomarker usage and imaging methods).

  • Support the development of TA-specific Quality Assurance plans that are risk based and efficient. This includes protocol specific audit plans, and the execution of audits using various methods (e.g., remote, or on-site).

  • Support Clinical Trial Teams for all quality management activities, including management of quality events (e.g., Deviations/CAPAs, Serious Breaches/Privacy Issues, Inspection Readiness activities, and Inspection Management).

  • Actively seek and implement innovative and proactive quality oversight methodologies (e.g., risk-based, data analytics that may leverage AI and Natural Language Processing, or other statistically based methods).

  • Review clinical trial protocols ensuring simplification, application of lessons learned, and identification of critical data and processes for risk management activities.

Key Capabilities

  • Maintain knowledge of current regulatory and quality practices/issues and provide continuous training and education​

  • Establish proven track record of GCP expertise and is able to provide advice on complex issues​

  • Technical knowledge of at least one R&D audit specialty area​

  • Knowledge of R&D function and business principles​

  • Applies analytical skills to evaluate and interpret Quality situations/issues using multiple sources of information, including qualitative, quantitative and trend data​

  • Works under minimal direction and independently determines R&D Quality approach that are thorough, practical and consistent with the R&D Quality TA program​

  • Manages multiple assignments​

  • Meets timelines for the reporting of R&D audits and other activities​

  • Communicate effectively locally, regionally and globally​

  • In-depth disciplinary knowledge; leverages business acumen and subject matter expertise​

  • Employs project management techniques​

  • In-depth understanding of company, regional and country goals​

  • Provide coaching /mentoring to staff and provide cross training for staff in area of expertise​​

  • Support achievement of departmental goals​​

Knowledge​

  • Through understanding of Clinical R&D activities and Global Regulations ​

  • Thorough Knowledge and application of international requirements of Good Clinical Practice(GCP) and/or Good Pharmacovigilance Practice (GPV) (required)​

  • Through knowledge of R&D processes and operations​

  • Knowledge of the Regulatory Submission and Inspection Management procedures.​

  • Quality Oversight of Clinical Trials, including clinical trial protocol development, execution, and submissions.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The dynamic professional we seek is an individual with these qualifications.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Doctorate degree and 2 years of Quality, Operations, and/or Regulatory Compliance experience within the Pharma/Biotech sector OR

  • Master’s degree and 4 years of Quality, Operations, and/or Regulatory Compliance experience within the Pharma/Biotech sector OR

  • Bachelor’s degree and 6 years of Quality, Operations, and/or Regulatory Compliance experience within the Pharma/Biotech sector OR

  • Associate’s degree and 10 years of Quality, Operations, and/or Regulatory Compliance experience within the Pharma/Biotech sector OR

  • High school diploma / GED and 12 years of Quality, Operations, and/or Regulatory Compliance experience within the Pharma/Biotech sector

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor of Science degree in appropriate discipline ​

  • Advanced degree (e.g., Master’s degree or PhD) ​

  • Quality Assurance Qualification/Certification​​

  • Minimum of 7 years in biopharmaceutical industry experience in Quality Management, Quality Assurance, or other relevant areas of the pharmaceutical/biotech industry where risk-based quality and quality by design are a core responsibility.​

  • Minimum of 5 years’ experience as an auditor, preferably in Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) and/or Good Pharmacovigilance Practice (GPvP)​

  • Experience supporting regulatory authority inspections of clinical research, and/or pharmacovigilance activities​

  • Leadership or mentoring experience ​

  • Oversight and implementation of Quality Management Systems and experience managing quality in electronic QMS such as Veeva or Trackwise.​

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including strong business writing abilities and active listening.

  • Ability to transform business and stakeholder feedback into clear, efficient processes using a straightforward language and format.

  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and decision-making abilities.

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

Job Title: Director, Central Quality Audit, Pharmacovigilance

Job Location: Remote

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Description Summary

Managing, ensuring and improving capabilities to comply with external standards and regulations. Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may influence work.

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Own the Pharmacovigilance (PV) Audit Program: Develop, implement, and maintain the global PV audit strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations (e.g., EMA, FDA, MHRA, PMDA) and industry best practices.
  • Manage Audit Operations: Oversee scheduling, planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up for PV audits, including internal audits and audits of service providers and affiliates. Fully participate in the audit program; actively owning and executing PV audits.
  • Risk Identification and Communication: Identify high-risk compliance issues, escalate findings, and provide actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
  • Regulatory Inspection Support: Prepare for and support PV-related health authority inspections, including back-room management and post-inspection follow-up.
  • Metrics and Reporting: Define and track PV audit KPIs, ensuring visibility of compliance risks and trends to leadership.
  • System Ownership: Manage audit-related modules within the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), including support of configuration, UAT, and documentation.
  • Team Leadership: Lead and develop a team of 3–5 auditors, providing coaching, mentorship, and performance management.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with PV Operations, Quality, and Regulatory teams to ensure audit outcomes drive continuous improvement.
  • Strategic Influence: Contribute to policy development and influence PV compliance strategy across the organization.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum 5 years of people leadership experience, including team development and performance management.
  • Qualified Lead Auditor with active certification.
  • Master’s degree and 5+ years in pharmacovigilance or pharmaceutical industry; or Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years relevant experience.
  • Minimum of 5 years’ experience driving Global programs to resolve quality compliance issues (directly).
  • Experience with Pharmaceutical QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to cGMP, GDP, GPvP, GCP and GLP.

Desired Characteristics

  • Experience with Medical Device QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to FDA CFR 21 820 and ISO 13485.
  • Prior Veeva and TrackWise Digital experience a plus.
  • Prior health authority experience a plus.

Job title: Head of Business Development, Europe (m/w/d)

Location: Germany (Munich or Düsseldorf preferred) — remote, with regular travel across Europe. Candidates based in the United Kingdom or the Nordics will also be considered.

Employment type: Full-time, permanent

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Compensation: Competitive base salary and uncapped performance-related variable compensation, benchmarked above market for the region. We will share the specific range with you in our first conversation, before any interview. We will not ask you about your current or previous salary at any stage.

Role Overview

Lumenci is seeking a Head of Business Development, Europe (m/w/d) to establish and scale our commercial presence across the European market, spanning both Lumenci's expert IP services and , our expert-guided AI platform for patent intelligence and monetisation.

This is a founding, revenue-owning role. You will be Lumenci's first dedicated business development leader in Europe, responsible for market entry, pipeline generation from a standing start, and closing the first wave of European clients across corporate IP departments, law firms, and litigation funders.

The role reports directly to the CEO and sits at the intersection of enterprise sales, IP domain expertise, product go-to-market, and regional market building. It is a senior individual contributor position carrying a personal revenue target, with the autonomy and executive access to match. Over time, this role will help define and build the European commercial function, including establishing repeatable market-entry processes and, as the region scales, contributing to future team structure and hiring.

You will work cross-functionally with our technical experts, consulting delivery teams, product leadership, and marketing to translate deep technical IP capability into European client relationships and recurring revenue.

About Lumenci

Founded in 2018, Lumenci is a premier intellectual property consulting firm specialising in patent litigation, expert witness testimony, and patent monetisation for leading corporations and global law firms across the software, telecommunications, semiconductor, and emerging technology sectors.

A key part of our model is the integration of deep technical expertise with litigation strategy. Our teams support high-stakes disputes by developing technical narratives, performing rigorous analysis, and partnering with world-class expert witnesses whose testimony shapes case outcomes in courts and arbitration forums worldwide. Alongside our services business, our iLumos platform delivers expert-guided AI for patent intelligence — portfolio segmentation, target identification, and infringement and validity assessment — moving clients from analysis to action in minutes rather than months.

Today we work with more than 175 clients and 80 law firms, supported by over 100 technical experts and 300+ campaigns, with more than $3.5B tied to verdicts, settlements, and negotiated outcomes.

Headquartered in Austin, Texas, with offices in San Francisco, New York, and Gurugram, India, Lumenci delivers end-to-end support spanning technical analysis, expert strategy, valuation, and monetisation execution. We are backed by VSS Capital Partners and Century Equity Partners.

We have built a strong North American franchise. Europe is our next market, and this is the role that opens it.

Key Responsibilities

Market entry and go-to-market strategy

  • Define and execute the go-to-market plan for Europe, beginning with the DACH region and expanding into the UK, Nordics, and broader EU markets.

  • Define ideal customer profiles, target account lists, and high-value early adopter segments for the European market.

  • Contribute to product positioning, messaging, and commercialisation strategy for both Lumenci services and iLumos, based on European customer and market feedback.

  • Gather structured market intelligence, customer discovery insights, and competitive observations — including UPC-driven shifts in European patent strategy — to inform roadmap and go-to-market decisions.

  • Advise leadership on entity, partner, and hiring decisions as Europe moves from beachhead to scaled operation.

New business development and enterprise sales

  • Own the full enterprise sales cycle for the region: territory and account planning, outbound prospecting, discovery, solution shaping with technical experts, commercial negotiation, and close.

  • Build durable executive relationships with Chief IP Counsel, Heads of Patents, General Counsel, Heads of Licensing, R&D and innovation leaders, and IP partners at leading European firms.

  • Build the region's pipeline through targeted outbound, referral networks, and a deliberate industry-event strategy across the European IP and licensing calendar.

  • Structure complex, multi-year engagements spanning litigation support, portfolio and licensing programmes, technical analysis, and AI-enabled IP platform services.

Platform commercialisation and pilots

  • Lead tailored iLumos demonstrations, workflow walkthroughs, and value-based conversations with European law firms, corporate IP teams, and litigation funders.

  • Structure pilot and proof-of-concept engagements with clear business objectives, success criteria, stakeholders, and timelines.

  • Support conversion of pilots and early engagements into subscription, usage-based, or long-term commercial relationships.

  • Stay engaged through early adoption on your first European accounts, partnering with product leadership and consulting delivery on onboarding, enablement, and value realisation until the region supports dedicated customer success coverage.

Commercial infrastructure

  • Establish the CRM discipline, forecasting cadence, and pipeline reporting rigour that the region will scale on, in partnership with global revenue operations.

  • Build repeatable market-entry, prospecting, and deal-structuring playbooks that support expansion into additional European markets.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally across product, engineering, consulting, sales, and executive leadership teams spanning US, European, and Indian operations.

Who You Are

You are a domain-deep, entrepreneurial enterprise seller who has built a market rather than inherited one. You are equally credible in a discovery conversation with a Head of Patents, a technical scoping session with reverse-engineering experts, a platform demonstration with end users, and a commercial negotiation with procurement.

You understand that in IP services and patent intelligence, trust and technical credibility precede transactions, and you have both the network and the substance to earn them. You are comfortable with the ambiguity of a first-in-region role, and you would rather own the outcome than inherit the infrastructure.

Required Qualifications

  • Extensive experience — typically 12 years or more — in enterprise business development or complex solution sales, with a sustained record of new-logo acquisition and target overachievement against seven-figure annual revenue goals.

  • Direct experience selling into intellectual property, legal, or professional services buyers — corporate IP and legal departments, and/or IP law firms.

  • Demonstrated success building a market, territory, or region from a standing start rather than inheriting an established book of business.

  • Proven ability to sell consultative, high-consideration engagements with long sales cycles and multiple stakeholders, including procurement and legal.

  • Experience running discovery conversations, guiding product demonstrations or capability presentations, and translating customer needs into solution workflows and quantified business value.

  • Established European network across the IP, licensing, or legal services community.

  • Strong CRM discipline and forecasting rigour, with the ability to establish commercial infrastructure without dedicated support.

  • Business-fluent English, plus business-fluent German or another major European business language aligned to your territory.

  • Legally authorised to work in your country of residence within Europe, and willing to travel extensively across the region.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience at an IP intelligence, legal technology, expert services, patent analytics, or IP managed services provider.

  • Technical fluency in one or more of: semiconductors, telecommunications and standards, AI/ML and cloud, software, consumer electronics, or medical devices.

  • Experience selling AI-enabled or platform-based products alongside expert human delivery.

  • Experience helping launch or commercialise a new product, business line, or geographic market.

  • Familiarity with patent monetisation, licensing programmes, or litigation funding economics.

  • Active participation in the European IP community — LES, AIPPI, EPO and UPC-adjacent events, IP Service World, IPBC, or similar.

  • Comfort operating in a founder-led, high-growth, distributed environment across US, European, and Indian teams.

What We Offer

  • Direct reporting line to the CEO, with genuine ownership of a region rather than a territory within an existing structure.

  • Base salary and on-target earnings as stated above, with uncapped variable compensation and accelerators above target.

  • A guaranteed variable component during your ramp period, reflecting that this is a market-entry role with no existing pipeline.

  • The scope and visibility of a founding commercial role in a private-equity-backed, high-growth business.

  • Remote working with a dedicated travel and industry-event budget.

  • 30 days of annual leave, plus public holidays and local benefits appropriate to your country of employment.

Recruitment Process

  1. Introductory conversation with People Operations

  2. Interview with the Chief Executive Officer

  3. Market-entry working session, based on a plan you prepare

  4. Panel conversation with consulting delivery, technical experts, and marketing

  5. Final conversation and reference checks

Lumenci is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, gender identity, age, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, disability, sexual orientation, marital or family status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law, including the German General Equal Treatment Act (AGG) and the UK Equality Act 2010. Selection decisions are based solely on qualifications, experience, and demonstrated capability.

You are not required to include a photograph, your date of birth, your age, your marital status, your nationality, or details of your health in your application, and we ask that you do not do so. We will not ask you about your current or previous salary at any stage of this process.

How Your Data Is Handled

Lumenci is the data controller for personal data you submit as part of this application. We process your data on the basis of our legitimate interest in assessing candidates and taking steps prior to entering into a contract of employment.

Your data will be used solely to assess your application, will be shared internally only with those involved in this recruitment process, and will be stored in our applicant tracking system. IPinfo New Business Sales Job Specification

About IPinfo

IPinfo was founded on a simple belief: IP data should be accurate, accessible, and reliable. Today, organizations around the world — from fast-growing startups to global enterprises — rely on our data to reduce risk, stop fraud, and better understand the network traffic that powers both their own operations and their customers’ businesses.

Rather than depending solely on static or third-party sources, we validate and generate our data through weekly, factual internet measurements. This approach delivers industry-leading accurate and reliable IP intelligence, strengthened by billions of weekly lookups and a team of remote data engineers and researchers.

The data supports some of the most respected companies in technology and security, including Anthropic, Cisco, Cloudflare, Datadog, Docker, Google, Mastercard, Microsoft, OpenAI, Snowflake, Censys, and Barracuda — organizations that depend on our scale and precision for mission-critical security, compliance, and operational workflows.

Whether helping a cybersecurity platform block threats, enabling a fintech provider to meet compliance requirements, or assisting an enterprise fraud team in preventing abuse, we provide the clarity needed to make confident, informed decisions.

    1. Share practical experience selling IPinfo data and actively contribute to elevating sales best practices

If this opportunity aligns with your experience and ambitions, we encourage you to apply.
